dataset_title: Seasonal roadside-grass dry co-digestion pilot evidence from André et al. (2019), abstract-level transcription
source_title: Dry anaerobic co-digestion of roadside grass and cattle manure at a 60 L batch pilot scale
license: No reuse license identified in accessible metadata; only factual abstract-level observations are transcribed.
data_basis: The abstract describes laboratory methane-potential measurements in June and October 2016 and 60 L dry-batch pilot co-digestion of roadside grass with solid cattle manure. Values and denominators are retained as reported; no conversions or model fitting are performed.
applicability: Reference-only Phase 5 evidence for the seasonality and operability of roadside-grass/manure dry digestion. It is not evidence for GreenHub post-protein residual digestion, grass-only methane yield, or Dutch supply performance.
limitations: The abstract does not fully identify the substrate-to-value mapping for each seasonal methane-potential result; the June/October association follows the abstract's stated order and is flagged for full-text confirmation.
The abstract does not give replicate counts, uncertainty, complete BMP protocol, feed characterization, loading, temperature, batch duration, or pilot working volume.
The inhibition-associated 34.8–44.4 Nm3 CH4/t VS range is not defined as a loss, yield, or specific response; it is retained as text and not used quantitatively.
The pilot compares layered filling with a mixed blend, but configuration-specific yields are absent from the abstract.
No values are transferred to GreenHub defaults, kinetic parameters, annual production, or Pareto scenarios.
retrieval_and_transcription_note: Primary article DOI and PubMed abstract cross-checked. Full text was not available through the accessible publisher page; unresolved substrate attribution is kept explicit.
